newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale sees deep divide over Canadian Wheat Board.
newsitem.headline: Goodale sees deep divide over Canadian Wheat Board.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Monday farmers were deeply divided over whether the Canadian Wheat Board monopoly should be diluted.
"It's pretty clear that on a number of very key issues, the opinions of farmers are very sharply divided," Goodale told reporters.
"The deepest divisions appear to be on...what would or would not appropriately be within the jurisdiction of the Canadian Wheat Board."
Goodale said previously he would need a clear consensus among farmers to end the board's monopoly.
"The possibility of a broad producer consensus appears remote," Goodale said on Monday.
He repeated his intention to announce the government's plans before Canadian Thanksgiving Day, which falls on October 14 this year.

The government-appointed Western Grain Marketing Panel recommended removing the CWB's monopoly on feed barley exports, pricing up to a quarter of milling wheat on the spot market and revamping the agency's corporate structure.
Goodale has declined to divulge his plans but has hinted that he would focus only on how the board was run.
